specTitle: NCD Care Companion — Backlog (Notifications + Error Boundaries)

tasks.title: Add notification types and fixture data

userStory.action: import CareCompanionNotification type and NOTIFICATION_TYPE const to type my component props and filter notifications
userStory.benefit: type-safe notification handling with autocomplete for all 7 notification types
userStory.context: Engineer is about to build the notification feed page and MSW handlers. Needs types first so everything downstream is typed correctly
userStory.interactionDetail: Engineer imports NOTIFICATION_TYPE and CareCompanionNotification from @/types/care-companion. Uses NOTIFICATION_TYPE keys for switch statements. Fixture file provides seed data for MSW handlers

tasks.description: Add NOTIFICATION_TYPE const object (7 types) and CareCompanionNotification interface to src/types/care-companion.ts. Deep-links must match existing routes: REFILL_REMINDER/REFILL_OVERDUE → /patients/care-companion/refill-schedule, REFILL_LOAN_OFFER/PREDICTIVE_CREDIT_OFFER → /patients/care-companion/medication-loan, EDUCATION_WEEKLY → /patients/care-companion/education, MEDICATION_CARD_AVAILABLE → /patients/care-companion/medication-cards, LAB_REMINDER → /patients/care-companion. Read existing types in src/types/care-companion.ts and existing fixtures in src/mocks/fixtures/ for patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: NOTIFICATION_TYPE const with 7 keys exports from src/types/care-companion.ts
CareCompanionNotification interface exports from src/types/care-companion.ts with all required fields (id, type, title, body, deepLink, scheduledAt, sentAt, readAt, metadata)
notifications.json contains exactly 7 notifications, one per type
All deepLink values match existing route paths in the prototype
npm run build passes with no new type errors

tasks.title: Add MSW notification handlers

userStory.persona: Frontend engineer building the notification feed page
userStory.action: fetch notifications from the mock API and mark them as read
userStory.benefit: realistic API simulation for notification CRUD without a backend
userStory.context: Engineer needs working mock endpoints before building the React Query hook and feed page. Handlers should match the patterns in the existing carecompanion.ts handlers
userStory.interactionDetail: GET /api/care-companion/notifications returns sorted list. PATCH /api/care-companion/notifications/:id/read sets readAt. POST /api/care-companion/notifications/simulate creates a test notification

tasks.description: Create src/mocks/handlers/notifications.ts with 3 MSW handlers: GET /api/care-companion/notifications (returns all notifications sorted by scheduledAt desc, supports ?unreadOnly=true filter), PATCH /api/care-companion/notifications/:id/read (marks notification as read by setting readAt to current ISO timestamp), POST /api/care-companion/notifications/simulate (dev-only, creates a notification of the given type and returns it). Import and register handlers in src/mocks/handlers/index.ts. Read src/mocks/handlers/carecompanion.ts for the exact MSW v2 handler pattern used in this codebase. Use domain module pattern: create notification helpers in src/mocks/domain/careCompanion.ts or a new notifications domain module.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/care-companion/notifications handler exists and returns CareCompanionNotification[]
PATCH /api/care-companion/notifications/:id/read handler exists and updates readAt
POST /api/care-companion/notifications/simulate handler exists
Handlers are registered in src/mocks/handlers/index.ts
npm run build passes with no new type errors

tasks.title: Create SectionErrorBoundary and EmergencyCardStaticFallback components

userStory.persona: Grace, a 52-year-old diabetic patient in Nairobi
userStory.action: continue using the care companion home screen even when one section fails to load
userStory.benefit: I never lose access to my emergency card or other sections because of a crash in an unrelated section
userStory.context: Grace opens care companion home. If the cost tracker section has a rendering bug, the rest of the page (refill schedule, emergency card, education) should still work. The emergency card section specifically must never show a generic error — it falls back to static emergency numbers
userStory.interactionDetail: Grace sees the care companion home with all 4 sections. If cost tracker crashes, that section shows 'Unable to load Cost Tracker' with a Retry button. She taps Retry and the section reloads. If the emergency card section crashes, she sees a static card with emergency numbers (999, 112, 0800 723 253) instead of a generic error
edgeCases: Multiple sections crash simultaneously — each shows its own fallback independently
Emergency card static fallback must be useful without any API data

tasks.description: Create SectionErrorBoundary at src/Routes/Patient/Pages/CareCompanion/components/SectionErrorBoundary.tsx. This is a React class component (error boundaries require componentDidCatch). Props: sectionName: string, children: ReactNode, fallbackContent?: ReactNode. On error: renders a card with 'Unable to load {sectionName}' message and a Retry button that resets error state. Uses bg-muted and text-muted-foreground tokens. Logs error to console (Sentry integration can be added later). Create EmergencyCardStaticFallback at src/Routes/Patient/Pages/CareCompanion/components/EmergencyCardStaticFallback.tsx. Renders a hardcoded emergency card for GENERAL condition with emergency numbers 999, 112, 0800 723 253. Read existing components in the CareCompanion directory for styling patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: SectionErrorBoundary exports from its file and accepts sectionName, children, and optional fallbackContent props
When a child throws, SectionErrorBoundary renders 'Unable to load {sectionName}' with a Retry button
Retry button resets error state and re-renders children
EmergencyCardStaticFallback renders emergency numbers 999, 112, 0800 723 253
Both components use Tailwind design tokens, not hardcoded colors
npm run build passes

tasks.title: Create NotificationFeedPage with route

userStory.persona: Grace, a 52-year-old diabetic patient in Nairobi
userStory.action: view all my care companion notifications in one place and tap to navigate to the relevant page
userStory.benefit: I never miss a refill reminder, education tip, or loan offer because notifications are centralized and actionable
userStory.context: Grace navigates to the notifications tab from the care companion. She sees notifications grouped by date. Unread ones have a teal dot. She taps a refill reminder notification — it marks as read and takes her to the refill schedule page
userStory.interactionDetail: Grace sees a list of notification cards grouped by date headers (Today, Yesterday, Earlier). Each card shows title, body preview, and a teal dot if unread. She taps a REFILL_REMINDER card. The teal dot disappears (mark read API fires) and she navigates to /patients/care-companion/refill-schedule. Back on the notifications page, the card no longer shows the dot
edgeCases: No notifications — show empty state with illustration
All notifications read — no teal dots visible
Network error marking as read — notification still navigates but dot remains

tasks.description: Create NotificationFeedPage at src/Routes/Patient/Pages/CareCompanion/Notifications/NotificationFeedPage.tsx. Lists all notifications grouped by date (Today, Yesterday, Earlier). Unread notifications show a teal dot (bg-accent). Tapping a notification: (1) calls mark-read mutation, (2) navigates to deepLink using react-router useNavigate. Empty state shows 'No notifications yet' message. Add lazy route at /patients/care-companion/notifications in the care companion route config. Read the existing page components (RefillSchedulePage, EducationFeedPage) for layout and styling patterns. Use React Query for data fetching (the hook will be created in the next phase, so use direct useQuery for now or create a simple inline fetch).
acceptanceCriteria: NotificationFeedPage renders at /patients/care-companion/notifications
Notifications are grouped by date (Today, Yesterday, Earlier)
Unread notifications show a teal dot indicator
Tapping a notification navigates to its deepLink path
Empty state renders when no notifications exist
Route is lazy-loaded in CareCompanionWrapper

tasks.title: Create notification React Query hooks

userStory.persona: Frontend engineer maintaining the notification feed page
userStory.action: use useNotifications() and useMarkNotificationRead() hooks to fetch and mutate notification data
userStory.benefit: consistent data fetching with automatic cache invalidation, loading states, and error handling
userStory.context: Engineer imports hooks into NotificationFeedPage. useNotifications fetches the list, useMarkNotificationRead provides a mutate function. On mark-read success, the notification list automatically refetches
userStory.interactionDetail: const { data: notifications, isLoading } = useNotifications(). const { mutate: markRead } = useMarkNotificationRead(). On tap: markRead(notificationId). List refetches automatically via query invalidation

tasks.description: Create src/Routes/Patient/Pages/CareCompanion/hooks/useNotifications.ts with two hooks: useNotifications(unreadOnly?: boolean) wraps useQuery fetching GET /api/care-companion/notifications with optional unreadOnly param. useMarkNotificationRead() wraps useMutation for PATCH /api/care-companion/notifications/:id/read, invalidates the notifications query key on success. Follow the exact pattern from existing hooks like useRefillSchedule.ts or useEducationFeed.ts. Then update NotificationFeedPage to use these hooks instead of any inline fetching.
acceptanceCriteria: useNotifications hook exports and returns { data, isLoading, error }
useNotifications accepts optional unreadOnly boolean parameter
useMarkNotificationRead hook exports and returns { mutate, isPending }
Mark-read success invalidates the notifications query key
NotificationFeedPage uses these hooks for data fetching
npm run build passes
